newsitem.title: USA: California's top trade official resigns - governor.
newsitem.headline: California's top trade official resigns - governor.

text.p: California's Secretary of Trade and Commerce Julie Meier Wright has resigned from state service and will be replaced by Lee Grissom, Gov. Pete Wilson said on Wednesday.
Wright, who held the top job at the state trade agency since 1991, will join the San Diego Regional Economic Development Corp as its president and chief executive officer.
Grissom will take over for Wright, 52, after August 1.

Grissom, 54, has served as director of the governor's office of planning and research since 1993. As director, he has been a top advisor to the governor on international trade and domestic economic issues.
His salary at the Trade and Commerce Agency will be $115,083 per year. The appointment is still subject to Senate confirmation.
The agency promotes economic development and investment in California. The secretary of the agency advises the governor on trade issues.
